title: MDN brain descending neurons coordinately activate backward and inhibit forward locomotion.
source_locator: Figure 8C-F; Results 'MDNs persist through metamorphosis and induce backward walking in adults'
quote: We observed light-induced backward walking in 8 of 10 adult flies assayed (Figure 8D; Video 5)
mapping_basis: Paper names the adult neurons MDN / moonwalker descending neurons; MDN is a MANC type in type_list.csv (synonym DNp50).
stimulation: 0.28 mW/mm2 red light, 10 s (after 10 s no light), three repeats per fly
other_cell_types: unnamed off-target projection visible in Figure 8F (green line)
notes: Intersection of larval MDN line (Split3, ss01613) with adult moonwalker line VT044845-lexA immortalises ReaChR in larval MDNs; backward walking scored by eye within 2 s of light onset. Backward walking coded yes for all three leg pairs per PROTOCOL section 3. Walking direction reverses to backward; the effect_on_walking vocabulary has no term for reversal, so not_assessed is used.

title: MDN brain descending neurons coordinately activate backward and inhibit forward locomotion.
source_locator: Figure 8G-I; Results 'MDNs persist through metamorphosis and induce backward walking in adults'
quote: all grew into adults that showed Chrimson-induced backward walking (n = 20; Figure 8H)
mapping_basis: Paper names the adult neurons MDN / moonwalker descending neurons and shows they match adult moonwalker morphology; MDN is a MANC type in type_list.csv.
stimulation: 617 nm LED, ~4.6 uW/mm2, fly in a 10-ml serological pipette
other_cell_types: four unnamed off-target neurons shown shaded blue in Figure 8I
penetrance: all 20 larvae selected for backward crawling gave backward-walking adults
notes: RU486-induced FLP immortalisation of Split1 (R49F02-AD/R53F07-DBD) expression in first instar larvae, giving lexAop-CsChrimson in adult MDNs; adults selected for having crawled backward as larvae, so penetrance is conditional. Backward walking coded yes for all three leg pairs per PROTOCOL section 3; only MDNs were labelled in all stained brains.
